terms.gloss: what is to be done: the business in hand
terms.grammar: relative clause with the gerundive of agō; the tense of esse and the mood follow the sentence
evidence: Vives, Exercitātiō 20: is praescrībit aliīs quae sint agenda
terms.comment: Latin says what has to be done rather than naming a list: Quae hodiē agenda sunt?, what’s on today? The neuter plural agenda is the gerundive, the source of the English word, and is used as a noun only in later Latin.

terms.gloss: a written agenda, a list of business
evidence: Levi–Bini p. 44, s.v. ordine del giorno
terms.comment: For the paper itself. Classically index is a list or table of contents (Quint. 10.1.57; Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a motion or item laid before a meeting
evidence: Cic. Pis. 29: nōn modo āctiōnem aliquam aut relātiōnem (Lewis & Short)
Levi–Bini p. 44, s.v. ordine del giorno
terms.comment: The matter a presiding magistrate put to the senate (referre ad senātum): an item on a formal agenda, not a list of chores.

phrases.latin: lūdēmus lūdum, in quō ūnus ēligitur rēx; is praescrībit aliīs quae sint agenda
phrases.english: we’ll play the game where one of us is chosen king; he tells the others what is to be done

sources: Lewis & Short: ago · Lewis & Short: index · Lewis & Short: relatio
